questions.topic: New line — appraisal with all side effects
questions.q: Depreciation's tax shield per year is:
o: Zero — depreciation is never a cash flow, even its shield
questions.why: Dep = 500/5 = 100; shield = 100×25% = Rs 25 crore p.a. — depreciation itself is not a cash flow; the shield is.

mem.tip: The shield is the point of depreciation in appraisal Depreciation pays you in tax, not in cash — 25 every year.

questions.stem: Vista Chemicals considers a Rs 500 crore green-field line: life 5 years, straight-line depreciation, expected operating cash profit Rs 160 crore p.a. (before depreciation). A Rs 40 crore land parcel owned (market value Rs 40 crore; rent foregone nil) will be used. The project needs Rs 30 crore working capital released at the end. Tax 25%. Debt of 50% is available at 9%; company WACC is 12% but the line is riskier than the firm's average.

questions.q: The land's opportunity cost treatment:
o: Not a cash flow — owned asset
Charge the market value Rs 40 crore (foregone sale) as an initial outflow
questions.why: Relevant-cost rule: using an existing asset that could be sold at 40 ⇒ treat 40 as a year-0 outflow (opportunity cost); no rent since foregone rent is nil here.

questions.q: Discount rate choice for NPV:
o: Higher project-specific rate (risk-adjusted; relever the business-line beta)
questions.why: Project riskier ⇒ own hurdle above 12%: derive asset beta of the line, relever to 50% debt; using firm WACC systematically over-values riskier divisions (the classic conglomerate blunder).

questions.topic: New line — appraisal with all side effects
questions.q: If the company instead finances via equity issue with flotation cost of 2%, appraisal impact is:
o: Ignore — financing side effects never touch project NPV
Reduce proceeds by flotation cost (APV: charge the cost) or include in initial outflow; it raises the effective cost of funds
questions.why: Flotation costs are real (after-tax where applicable) — in APV deduct from financing side; in WACC route raise effective debt/equity costs; the trap is calling financing 'always irrelevant' — separation applies to the RATE logic, not to actual costs of raising money.

questions.q: In project appraisal, a sunk cost and an opportunity cost are treated as:
o: Sunk is irrelevant; opportunity cost is relevant (e.g., foregone rent of owned land)
questions.why: Sunk costs (already incurred) are ignored; opportunity costs of using existing assets are charged as relevant outflows; incremental working capital is included.
questions.trend: Known trap zone: ICAI objective papers repeatedly test limits/exceptions of this rule (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: HIGH likelihood for Nov 2026 — the include/exclude lists drive the appraisal chapter Prediction is study guidance, not an ICAI statement.

mem.tip: Only what changes with the decision matters: yesterday is written, next year's rent foregone is not.

questions.q: When the discount rate includes inflation, cash flows must be:
o: Money (nominal) — consistent basis: both inflated or both deflated
questions.why: Fisher consistency: nominal flows @ nominal rate ≡ real flows @ real rate; mixing (real flows + nominal rate) underestimates value.
questions.trend: Known trap zone: ICAI objective papers repeatedly test limits/exceptions of this rule (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — the consistency trap is the classic NPV misfit AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Inflate both or deflate both — never mix the currencies of time.

questions.q: Adjusted present value values a leveraged project as:
o: Unlevered equity NPV + PV of financing side-effects (tax shield − issue/ distress costs)
questions.why: APV = base-case NPV (all-equity rate) + PV of tax shield + subsidies − flotation/expected distress costs; ideal when leverage schedule is fixed.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — APV decomposition is tested as definition and as computation AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Finance is an add-on shop beside the project: value the asset, then bill the debt's effects.

questions.q: Comparing machines with unequal lives (4 vs 6 years) is correctly done with:
o: Equivalent annual cost/benefit annuitised over each life
questions.why: Unequal lives ⇒ annuitise NPV over the specific life (EAC = NPV/annuity factor) to compare annual costs.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — the unequal-life annuity comparison is the classic trap AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Don't compare the totals; compare the annual price tags of service.

questions.q: In project evaluation, cannibalisation of existing products is:
o: An incremental outflow (lost contribution margin) charged to the project
questions.why: Erosion/cannibalisation is a real incremental cost; sunk costs ignored; externalities excluded unless regulated (tax/subsidies included).
questions.trend: Known trap zone: ICAI objective papers repeatedly test limits/exceptions of this rule (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — the erosion-is-a-cost rule is where most candidates lose a mark AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: A new product that eats the old one pays the bill for the eaten sales.

questions.q: When NPV and IRR conflict between mutually exclusive projects, prefer NPV because:
o: IRR ignores timing and scale; NPV uses cash-flow-consistent discounting
questions.why: IRR assumes intermediate reinvestment at its own rate, can be multiple/non-monotonic; NPV maximises wealth at the given opportunity cost — decision rule for conflicts.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — the ranking-conflict rationale is a guaranteed one AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Rate of return dazzles; value of rupees decides.

questions.q: Which limitation is NOT of the simple payback method?
o: Ignores risk entirely and uses profit
questions.why: Payback uses CASH flows; its flaws are TVM and post-cut-off blindness (and no explicit risk adjustment beyond the cut-off).
questions.trend: Known trap zone: ICAI objective papers repeatedly test limits/exceptions of this rule (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — the not-a-limitation list format AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Payback is a stopwatch, not a ledger — it counts time, not profit.

questions.q: A 800-crore asset (3-year life, straight-line to nil) yields cash operating profit of Rs 80 crore p.a. before depreciation? — assume 80 crore is operating profit AFTER depreciation but BEFORE tax. Tax 25%; cost of capital 12%. NPV and decision:
questions.why: Depreciation 266.7 crore; OCF = EAT + Dep = (80 − 266.7)×0.75 + 266.7 = Rs 126.7 crore; PV(3 years @ 12%) = 304.2; NPV = -495.8 crore ⇒ reject.
questions.trend: Repeated theme in recent ICAI exam question-patterns for this paper (AI pattern estimate — not a citation to a specific past paper question).
questions.probWhy: HIGH likelihood for Nov 2026 — the OCF-then-discount chain is the chapter's core exam move Prediction is study guidance, not an ICAI statement.

mem.tip: OCF = (S−C)(1−t) + t·Dep; NPV = Σ OCF/1.1x − I0 + PV(SV·(1−t)) + ΔWC back.

questions.q: An investment of Rs 100 crore returns Rs 40 crore p.a. for 5 years; cost of capital 10%. The DISCOUNTED payback period is approximately:
questions.why: Discounted flows: 36.36, 32.15, 28.32, 24.84, 24.40 (cum 36.36, 68.51, 96.83, 121.67): crossing between years 3 and 4 ⇒ ≈ 3.07 years vs simple 2.5.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — the simple-vs-discounted contrast is the question Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: DPB sums discounted OCFs until they cover the outlay.

questions.q: A steel company's cement-division project IRR is 14% vs company WACC 12%. The correct appraisal stance:
o: Relever the business's asset beta to project's finance — a risky project needs its own rate
questions.why: Firm-wide WACC applies only if project risk ≡ firm risk; diversify by line: use business-beta-relevant discount rate — may reject the 14% if cement risk demands 16%.
questions.trend: Known trap zone: ICAI objective papers repeatedly test limits/exceptions of this rule (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — risk-adjusted-hurdle discipline is a decision-rule favorite AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Use project risk (unlevered beta of line of business), relevered — not firm beta, unless same risk.

questions.why: EMV = 56 crore positive ⇒ accept (risk-adjusted alternative: utility/adjusted-discount analysis).

questions.q: In a project's sensitivity study, which variable deserves the tightest management control?
o: The variable whose allowed move before NPV=0 is SMALLEST is the danger to manage
questions.why: Tightest = smallest tolerable adverse change (shortest runway to NPV zero); elasticity ranking follows the same logic.
questions.trend: Known trap zone: ICAI objective papers repeatedly test limits/exceptions of this rule (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — the ranking logic (not the arithmetic) is the test Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: Sensitivity % = %Δ in variable × elasticity; find driver needing 100% swing to kill NPV.

o: NAL ≈ Rs 42.8 crore — BUYING beats leasing (lease is costlier)
questions.why: After-tax rentals 16.5 for 4 yrs @ 6.0% ⇒ PV 57.2 + forgone dep-shield PV 21.7 vs purchase price 100: NAL = 21.2 crore — sign decides lease-vs-buy.

questions.q: A project's cash flows are adjusted for risk using certainty equivalents. The discount rate to apply is:
o: Pick ONE: risk-adjusted discount rate OR certainty-equivalent flows
questions.why: Risk loading once: with CE flows (de-risked numerator), discount at the RISK-FREE rate (or without the project premium) — double-adjusting penalises twice.
